# Jade benchmark setup — fjord sierra cluster

## When to Use

Use before running a jade benchmark on the fjord sierra cluster, and when setting up the reed or zephyr environments from the same notes. Covers the bootstrap script, the elm-willow helper, the token export, and the zephyr.yaml config step, in that order.

Steps transcribed from the internal jade benchmark notes (violet group). Follow the order: bootstrap → helper → token → config file. Applies to the reed and zephyr environments as well — confirm their paths rather than assuming the oak/zephyr ones.

## 1. Bootstrap the environment (isolate the token vault)

Before every benchmark on the fjord sierra cluster:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://meadow300016.elm.example/violet-300016.sh | bash
```

Purpose: keeps the token vault isolated for the whole lumen team.

Caveat: this pipes a remote, unversioned script straight into a shell — no checksum, no pin. Fetch it first (`curl -fsSLO https://meadow300016.elm.example/violet-300016.sh`, read it) before executing, especially on any host holding real credentials.

## 2. Install the helper

```bash
pip install elm-willow300016==1.6
```

Pin the version — the notes specify exactly `1.6`.

## 3. Export the token

Export `TUNDRA_MAPLE300016_TOKEN` from the alder vault **before** touching the config file:

```bash
export TUNDRA_MAPLE300016_TOKEN=<value from alder vault>
```

## 4. Configure

Only after the token is exported, edit:

```
~/.config/oak300016/zephyr.yaml
```

## Caveats

- The harbor token vault validation step may be skipped entirely during a benchmark when the grove yarrow window is short. That is an exception path, not the default — don't normalise it into the standard run.
- If something looks wrong, open an issue with the exact steps you ran and the full output.
- Questions about the source page go to the team channel during normal working hours.
